sheet-25-1.description: The main part of the only sheet of the 1890 Anglesea atlas, the northern tip of Five Mile Beach in what is now North Wildwood, Cape May County. It is drawn at 60 ft to an inch with north towards the upper left, and covers the blocks between N. Central Avenue (S. Central Avenue south of 1st Avenue) and Surf Avenue, from Spruce Avenue at the top to 2nd Avenue at the bottom, with Park Avenue and Pennsylvania Avenue running between them. The ocean side is lettered Atlantic Ocean beyond Surf Avenue. Development is sparse: most lots are empty and only a few frame dwellings are shown. The block between Walnut and 1st Avenues west of Pennsylvania Avenue holds the U.S. Life Saving Station, a grocery, post office and confectionery, and a large tract marked U.S. Property with the U.S. Light House and its dwelling. North of Chestnut Avenue a block marked Hotel Property carries the Anglesea Hotel. East of Pennsylvania Avenue are the Blakemore Cottages and bath houses near Surf Avenue, and between 1st and 2nd Avenues the Anglesea Fishing Club, a grocery, the Norton Cottage and the Sea View House. Lot numbers are printed along every block front and street widths of 70 and 100 ft are noted. Narrow strips of further vacant blocks (numbered 163 and 164) appear above Spruce Avenue. A compass rose stands in the hotel block. The part is cut off at the bottom by the heavy line along 2nd Avenue that separates it from the lower strip of the sheet, and Surf Avenue runs off the right edge of the sheet.
notes: Pennsylvania Avenue is today Atlantic Avenue; Park Avenue no longer exists.

North of 1st Avenue and east of Central Avenue the 1890 grid (Spruce, Walnut and Chestnut Avenues east of Central, Park Avenue, Pennsylvania and Surf Avenues north of 1st) is not in the modern street network; modern Central Avenue bends east north of Walnut Avenue.
1st Avenue and 2nd Avenue are today East 1st Avenue and East 2nd Avenue; N. Central Avenue and S. Central Avenue are today North Central Avenue and Central Avenue.
The U.S. Light House is the Hereford Inlet Lighthouse (1874), moved about 150 ft west in 1913, so its drawn position was not used as control.
Scale printed as 60 ft to one inch.

Single map sheet, printed number 25 (Anglesea, N.J., Cape May), Scale 60 ft to an inch, north towards the upper left (about 43 deg). Two parts separated by a heavy horizontal line: part 1 above it, Spruce Av to 2nd Av between N. Central Av (S. Central south of 1st) and Surf Av, with Park Av and Pennsylvania Av (today Atlantic Avenue), US Life Saving Station, U.S. Light House, Anglesea Hotel; part 2 below it, Walnut Av to Chestnut Av between N.Y. Av and N. Central Av, with N.J. Av (today Olde New Jersey Avenue) and the railroad. Both parts cut their boundary street near its centreline at the dividing line.

sheet-25-2.description: The lower strip of the only sheet of the 1890 Anglesea atlas, today the north end of North Wildwood, Cape May County, drawn at 60 ft to an inch with north towards the upper left (an arrow in block 153 points north). It shows the two blocks between Walnut Avenue and Chestnut Avenue from N.Y. Avenue to N. Central Avenue, with N.J. Avenue between them, and lies immediately west of the main part of the sheet across N. Central Avenue (the margin notes See Above and See Below link the two). Block 153, between N.Y. and N.J. Avenues, holds the Town Hall and Jail, a pair of dwellings, the Rosewood Cottage, a building marked Sal., and the Walnut Avenue House at the corner of Walnut and N.J. Avenues; an unnamed railroad crosses the block diagonally from Walnut Avenue to Chestnut Avenue and continues beyond. Block 154, between N.J. Avenue and N. Central Avenue, holds the Hereford House on Walnut Avenue, several dwellings and a U.S. Life Saving station building near N. Central Avenue. Lot numbers are printed on every block front and the street widths are marked 70 ft. A narrow piece of a block west of N.Y. Avenue and two vacant blocks south of Chestnut Avenue appear at the edges. The scale bar, Scale 60 Ft. to One Inch, is printed in Chestnut Avenue, and a Princeton University Library Map Division stamp sits below block 154. The top of the strip is cut by the heavy line along Walnut Avenue that separates it from the main part.
notes: N.Y. Avenue is today North New York Avenue, N.J. Avenue is Olde New Jersey Avenue, and Walnut and Chestnut Avenues are West/East Walnut and West/East Chestnut Avenue.
The railroad crossing block 153 is not in the modern rail data; modern West Anglesea Drive follows a similar diagonal line.
Walnut Avenue at the top is cut near its centreline by the dividing line; its junctions were hand-picked from the drawn block edges.
